content.user_title: Build React Native Features with Proven Patterns
content.value_statement: React Native features can become difficult to maintain when component and state patterns are inconsistent. This skill provides focused examples for building, refactoring, and reviewing mobile application code.
actual_capabilities: Shows custom hook, compound component, and render prop patterns.
Explains local, context-based, and Zustand state management examples.
Provides an async data-loading hook with loading, error, and cleanup handling.
Demonstrates memoization and lazy-loading patterns for React components.
Covers error boundaries, typed error handling, safe areas, and keyboard avoidance.
limitations: It provides examples and guidance, not a complete application architecture.
It does not install dependencies or run tests.
It does not cover platform-specific native module implementation.
Examples may need adaptation for your React Native version and project conventions.

use_cases.title: Build a reusable screen feature
use_cases.description: Choose component, state, and data-loading patterns for a new React Native screen.

use_cases.title: Refactor a large component
use_cases.description: Split a complex component into custom hooks, focused children, and shared state boundaries.

use_cases.title: Review application reliability
use_cases.description: Check loading states, error handling, cleanup, safe-area handling, and keyboard behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a simple state pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a React Native counter and settings screen. Recommend the simplest state pattern and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Create a data-loading hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React Native hook that loads a user by ID and handles loading, errors, cancellation, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a feature screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Native screen design. Propose component boundaries, custom hooks, and a state management approach that reduces prop drilling.

prompt_templates.title: Improve performance deliberately
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this React Native list screen for measurable performance issues. Recommend memoization or lazy loading only where the expected benefit is clear.

output_examples.input: I need to share theme settings across several screens.
output: Recommendation: use React Context for this cross-cutting concern.
Create a provider near the application root.
Expose a typed hook so consumers fail clearly outside the provider.

output_examples.input: My user profile screen loads data after navigation.
output: Recommendation: use a custom data-loading hook.
Track loading and error state with the result.
Cancel state updates when the screen unmounts.

output_examples.input: A screen has grown beyond 300 lines.
output: Identify separate display, data, and interaction responsibilities.
Extract shared behavior into custom hooks.
Keep optimization changes tied to a measured performance concern.

best_practices: Start with local state and add shared state only when multiple components need it.
Handle loading, error, and cleanup paths for every asynchronous operation.
Measure performance before adding memoization or lazy loading.
anti_patterns: Do not create large components with unrelated responsibilities.
Do not mutate React state directly.
Do not omit cleanup for effects that can update state after unmounting.

faq.question: Which state pattern should I use first?
faq.answer: Use local state first. Use context or a store when state must be shared across component boundaries.

faq.question: Does this skill require Zustand?
faq.answer: No. Zustand is shown as one global state option, but the skill also covers local state and React Context.

faq.question: Can I use these patterns in an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply the patterns incrementally while preserving your project conventions and dependency choices.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete mobile application?
faq.answer: No. It provides reusable examples and guidance for targeted implementation and refactoring work.

faq.question: Does it help with performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers memoization and lazy loading, with guidance to profile before optimizing.

faq.question: Does it cover native iOS and Android modules?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on React Native component and application-level patterns.
